On Mon, May 31, 2027 at 09:08 AM Elena Morales <elena@brightcart.com> wrote:
> Attached is our Q2 usage export...

Thanks for sending this, Elena — helpful snapshot. I pulled a quick pass and highlighted three practical takeaways for the renewal conversation:

- Consumption drivers: ~62% of incremental tokens in Apr were repeated prefix calls from one service; with targeted prefix/KV caching we estimate a 15–22% permanent reduction in monthly token spend.
- Latency correlation: the 95th-percentile blips align to short burst windows where concurrency exceeded current reserved lanes; smoothing with a small burst capacity reduces tail latency without raising baseline cost too much.
- Contract option: recommend an 18-month staged-commit (40/60 split) + 90-day canary to validate prefetch and batching improvements. This balances economics and gives you runway for product changes.

I've attached a simple economic model (Redwood_Econ_Model_BC-4372.xlsx) that overlays the three options I think we should present. Looping in Ben for pricing and Monica for ops/lead time.

Proposed meeting: Wed Jun 2, 11:00 AM PT — does that work?

—Grace O'Connor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>

Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing & commit options (brightcart — BC-4372)

Elena / team,

Thanks for the data — below are three straightforward paths we can offer. Numbers in the sheet are monthly token equivalents and estimated $/token after discounts. See attached proposed-addendum-v1.docx for addendum language we can start on.

Tier A — Conservative
- 12 month term
- Reserve 25% of current run-rate
- Burst credits available at 2x baseline price
- No up-front fee
Estimated annual savings vs on-demand: ~6%

Tier B — Recommended (Flex Uplift)
- 18 month term
- Reserve 40% of current run-rate (staged: 20% immediate, 20% at month 7)
- 30-day canary at current commit + 10% burst lane for two weeks
- Moderate up-front credit to offset implementation
Estimated annual savings: 14–19% (depends on realized caching)

Tier C — Aggressive
- 24 month term
- Reserve 60% run-rate + dedicated pool for latency-sensitive endpoints
- Lower per-token rate, 3-month SLA credit window
Estimated annual savings: 22–28%

We can wire a 30-day canary for Tier B starting at your existing commit. If you want the 90-day validation Grace suggested, we can extend the canary but that shifts staging dates.

Next steps I propose: Elena confirms preferred tier, we provision a pilot plan, legal prepares addendum (I attached a draft).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Ops notes for pilot & capacity (BrightCart)

Quick ops notes to align expectations:

- Lead times: Dedicated pool provisioning (if chosen) requires 4–6 weeks; burst lanes and prefetch rules can be applied within 72 hours for a small pilot.
- KV/prefix caching: We'll need a short integration window (1–2 sprints) to tag stable prefixes — engineering can run A/B for a week to measure delta.
- Monitoring: Redwood Console will give per-route latency and token breakdown. We'll add a temporary dashboard for BrightCart and share access.
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence is attached. For Private/VPC options, talk to security early — key exchange + network ACLs might add 2 weeks.

Attached: SOC2_summary.pdf

I'll prepare a short runbook for the 30-day canary and include rollback criteria (error rate, latency 95p crossing threshold, or >15% unexpected token burn).

—Monica
